The dates a window specification resolves to

Source: R/window_dates.R
window_dates.Rd

Turns a window from window_lag(), window_season(), window_calendar(), window_fixed() or window_since() into the dates it covers, for every location and interview date in data: one row per key, interview and lag.

Usage

window_dates(window, data, interview = NULL, by = NULL)

Arguments

window

A window from window_lag(), window_lags(), window_season(), window_calendar(), window_fixed() or window_since().

data

A data frame holding the key column, the interview dates, and the columns named by window where it names any.

interview

<data-masking> The column holding the interview date. Taken from the metadata after prepare_coord().

by

Name of the column linking data to the indicator table, as a string. Taken from data's metadata where it records a key.

Value

A tibble with one row per distinct key, interview date and lag: the key column under its own name, interview, lag (0 for the window closest to the interview, counting up as they recede), w_start and w_end.

Details

summarise_by_interview() resolves windows this way before summarising. The same resolution is exported here for the cases that do not go through a summary: cutting a daily series to each household's growing season, joining windows onto a table of one's own, or checking what a window actually covers before relying on it.

Windows are half-open, (w_start, w_end]: a day equal to w_start falls outside the window and a day equal to w_end falls inside it, so that consecutive lags of the same window neither overlap nor leave a gap.

Rows are dropped rather than returned with missing dates when they have no interview date, no key, or – for window_calendar() and window_since() – no bounds. Resolving a window is therefore not a row-preserving operation, and the result is distinct over the key and the interview date: households sharing both share a window.

The season bounds of window_calendar(), and the event date of window_since(), are not arguments here. The window object already records which columns of data hold them, so naming them twice is not possible.

See also

window_lag() for the window objects, summarise_by_interview() for summarising a series over them.

Examples

survey <- tibble::tibble(
    division  = c("a", "b"),
    interview = as.Date(c("2023-11-20", "2023-06-15")),
    sos       = c(92, 92),
    eos       = c(297, 297)
)

# the twelve months before each interview
window_dates(window_lag("1 year"), survey, interview, by = "division")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   division interview    lag w_start    w_end     
#>   <chr>    <date>     <int> <date>     <date>    
#> 1 a        2023-11-20     0 2022-11-20 2023-11-19
#> 2 b        2023-06-15     0 2022-06-15 2023-06-14

# the last growing season to have closed before each interview: division b
# was interviewed inside the 2023 season, so it takes 2022's
window_dates(window_calendar(sos, eos), survey, interview, by = "division")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   division interview    lag w_start    w_end     
#>   <chr>    <date>     <int> <date>     <date>    
#> 1 a        2023-11-20     0 2023-04-01 2023-10-24
#> 2 b        2023-06-15     0 2022-04-01 2022-10-24
